The acoustic guitar, also called the wooden guitar, is a fretted chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.322-5, in the lute family / plucked. Its resonator passes the string's vibration through the top, the bridge and the soundhole into the air inside the body and amplifies it; the standard six strings are tuned from low to high as E2, A2, D3, G3, B3, E4. The player plucks melody with a plectrum or the fingertips, or strums chords; in the jazz band and in acoustic playing it once competed with the banjo.
